economy.summary: Scanlon says Americans deserve a government willing to address the cost of living crisis, naming energy, housing, education, and health care as areas where affordability needs government action.
economy.short: Says government must address cost-of-living crisis: energy, housing, healthcare.

taxes.summary: Scanlon opposed the 2025 Republican tax-and-spending bill (One Big Beautiful Bill Act), which extended the 2017 tax cuts and reduced Medicaid spending; she disputed the GOP's justification of the bill and said looming cuts were already causing a medical center to announce closure.
taxes.short: Opposed 2025 Republican tax-and-spending bill, citing Medicaid cuts.

abortion.summary: Scanlon supports abortion access and defends the FACE Act's protections for clinic access; in a hearing statement she said all women deserve the freedom to work with their doctors and families to decide on the healthcare that's right for them.
abortion.short: Supports abortion access; defends FACE Act clinic-access protections.

education.summary: Scanlon opposes federal education funding cuts and supports Title I funding for public schools, saying Philadelphia-area schools are already underfunded and that cutting Title I would cost Philadelphia around 5,000 teachers.
education.short: Opposes federal education funding cuts; supports Title I funding.

healthcare.summary: Scanlon opposes Republican-proposed Medicaid cuts, saying they would threaten access to care for all Americans and push hospitals, nursing homes, and health clinics into bankruptcy.
healthcare.short: Opposes Medicaid cuts; says they threaten hospitals and care access.

energy.summary: Scanlon criticizes legislation that increases reliance on fossil fuels and rolls back electric vehicle subsidies, and opposes efforts to undo sustainable energy investments.
energy.short: Opposes fossil-fuel expansion and EV subsidy rollbacks; supports clean energy.

guns.summary: Scanlon supports a federal assault weapons ban, joining Philadelphia gun-control and public school advocates to call for one, and has cosponsored the Assault Weapons Ban of 2023 and the Bipartisan Background Checks Act of 2023.
guns.short: Supports federal assault weapons ban; cosponsored background-check legislation.

economy.summary: Manganaro says he is running for Congress to stop wasteful federal spending that he says is fueling inflation and causing hardship for average people.
economy.short: Says he will stop wasteful federal spending fueling inflation.

taxes.summary: Manganaro supports working across the aisle on a credible path to balance the federal budget, with oversight of federal spending, cost/benefit analysis before bills pass, and post-passage audits; he opposes new entitlement expansions.
taxes.short: Supports balancing budget and spending oversight; opposes entitlement expansions.

education.summary: Manganaro advocates school choice with per-child funding directed to parents, and raises concerns about boys and young men feeling alienated in schools.
education.short: Supports school choice with per-child funding for parents.

healthcare.summary: Manganaro opposes the Affordable Care Act's approach to healthcare and favors giving patients control through free-market mechanisms.
healthcare.short: Opposes ACA approach; favors free-market, patient-controlled healthcare.

energy.summary: Manganaro opposes the Regional Greenhouse Gas Initiative and supports an all-of-the-above energy policy including nuclear energy development and Pennsylvania hydrocarbon resources, while supporting environmental monitoring of drilling, fracking, and resource transportation.
energy.short: Opposes RGGI; supports all-of-the-above energy including nuclear, hydrocarbons.

guns.summary: Manganaro has said the Second Amendment is a good thing, citing the importance of individual self-defense.
guns.short: Supports Second Amendment, citing individual self-defense.
